quest.title: Time and Wind
quest.description: You reach an uninhabited island across the sea, which is home to an enigmatic sundial. Who knows what secret it holds?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Mora x60000

dialogues.speaker: Ravaged Carving
dialogues.text: "Stories brought on the wind will bloom into legends in due time."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does this even mean? ...Paimon has no idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, this place looks like it hides some secret...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's check this area out. We might find some clues!

dialogues.speaker: Ravaged Carving
dialogues.text: "Stories brought on the wind will bloom into legends in due time."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This must be the sundial mentioned in the notebook!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get what's special about it, though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we should read that notebook a bit more carefully.

talks.objective: Pursue the Eye of the Storm
Search for the Eye of the Storm

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: Hmm? Did you have some business here, Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Eye of the Storm...

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: An Eye of the Storm? I've been in this area this entire time, and I've never seen such a thing, except for that sudden huge gust wind earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: But I'm sure that it wasn't an Eye of the Storm. I would recognize one of those things anywhere.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Believe me, I wouldn't be able to forget something like that coming to interrupt my research even if I tried.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: To be precise, I'm doing research together with a friend of mine.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: He's also a scholar, and we went to Sumeru Akademiya together.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: He became an archaeologist thereafter, traveling the world and doing surveys, while I continued my studies in the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: When he came to Mondstadt, he told me excitedly that he was surveying the Thousand Winds Temple.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: He even said something like: "Once I've uncovered the secrets of your homeland, you're the first person I'll tell."

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: I didn't hear from him afterwards. I asked someone to send Cyrus a letter, requesting that the Adventurers' Guild help me look for my friend's whereabouts.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: But there was no news of him at all, and so I discontinued my studies and hurried back here.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: But there's nothing here but a sundial, and there are no other clues...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, there's a sundial on that island...

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: What? There's another sundial elsewhere that's identical to this one, and it's on an island?

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Oh, yes! Now I remember. I've actually seen that island sometimes, when the weather's clear.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Wait... You said that you found a notebook next to the sundial? Had my friend perhaps been there...?

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Thank you. If I have the chance, I will head to that island to have a look. For now, however, I still have to figure this place out.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: I must continue my research. If you're interested, you can have a look at my research notes. I've left them over there.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Who knows? Perhaps there's something in there that might help you.

choices.text: What are you up to here?

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Me? I'm doing a bit of research.

dialogues.speaker: Ravaged Carving
dialogues.text: "Stories brought on the wind will bloom into legends in due time."

talks.objective: Uncover the secret of the uninhabited island
Observe the shadow on the sundial
Defeat the Eye of the Storm

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: Where did this thing come from? It wasn't here before!

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: How did you summon it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's "time and wind..."

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: So, there's another sundial exactly like this one on the island, am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: And the method to solve its riddle is the same? Then there must be some link between these two sundials, and the two places they are located in.

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: I must find a way to get to that island, and quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: Thank you, Traveler. Once I've made some preparations, I will look for you, and we shall visit that uninhabited island together.

dialogues.speaker: Henry Morton
dialogues.text: Time and wind... Just what did he find?

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: Oh, that's something that my friend mentioned in the very last letter that he sent me.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: He said that "time and wind" hide one of Mondstadt's secrets.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: However, I've never heard that phrase before, and I'm from around these parts. Who knows where he heard that...

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: I did. Though I'm from Mondstadt, I've always been studying at the Sumeru Akademiya. I've probably spent more time there than I have in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: You want to know what happens in there? Well, it's not a secret, so... Hmm, how should I put it?

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: They're a bunch of weird people. Hmm, perhaps that's too disrespectful... I guess they're "people who make quite the impression?"

response.speaker: Henry Morton
response.text: If you ever have the chance to go, you'll see what I mean. But just stick to having a look. You don't want to stay too long.
